Hi Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying asks from legal/procurement before we move into procurement: 

- Controller vs Processor: please confirm in plain language that MedSys is the controller and Redwood is the processor for data processed by the hosted inference. If there are any exceptions (e.g., Redwood acts as controller for aggregated telemetry), call them out.

- Subprocessors: we need confirmation that every current subprocessors list participant has signed a DPA flow-down and that you will notify us 30 days prior to adding any new subprocessor (preferred). Is 30 days standard?

- Breach notification: procurement requires an explicit SLA for notification timing and the level of detail. We prefer 48 hours for initial notification; is that feasible or negotiable?

- Logging & evidence: we require forensic log exports covering request IDs, timestamps, model/route, and the KV cache identifiers for at least 180 days for our retention policy — can Redwood support this, and what are the costs?

- Residency: confirm that data-at-rest for the MedSys account can be restricted to US-East-only and that backups will not be replicated outside region without prior approval.

I've attached our standard DPA (MedSys_DPA_Template_v3.docx) so you can show any proposed changes inline.

Please cc Mark Hansen from BizOps (mark.hansen@medsys.io) on procurement and let me know if you want a short call to iron these items out.

Subject: Re: Fwd: MedSys privacy asks — need quick answers for Julia

Kim / team — quick bullets below you can send to Julia; legal notes in parentheses where sign-off required. Happy to jump on a 15m sync if needed.

1) Controller / Processor- Plain language: MedSys Health is the Controller; Redwood Inference acts as Processor for customer data processed through our hosted inference services. Redwood does collect limited operational telemetry (service metrics and aggregated usage) as controller for improving the service; telemetry does not include PII or customer prompt contents unless explicitly configured by the customer. (Legal: standard statement; any changes to telemetry collection must be documented in the addendum.)

2) Subprocessors- Current subprocessors list attached (subprocessors-202808.csv). All listed subprocessors have executed contractual flow-downs that include data protection obligations. Redwood provides advance notice of planned subprocessor additions; standard notice is 30 days. If MedSys requires a longer notice period, Legal can discuss a rolling exception for enterprise customers.

3) Breach notification- We can commit to initial notification within 72 hours for incidents materially affecting customer data. For customers with enterprise contracts, we will consider a 48-hour initial notification requirement on a case-by-case basis (requires Legal and Security sign-off). Full forensic report and root cause analysis will follow as investigations complete. (Legal: 48h is negotiable but may require compensating controls or insurance language.)

4) Logs & forensic exports- Default retention: 30 days. Options: 90 days (standard add-on) or 365 days (enterprise add-on). Exportable logs include request ID, timestamp, route/model, and system-level identifiers; we do not retain prompt contents unless customer enables request logging of payloads. For 180-day retention, estimate is +15% on token-storage-related billing (we will provide a precise quote via Sales Ops).

5) Residency & backups- We can pin account workloads and data-at-rest to US-EAST region. Backups are retained in-region by default and will not be replicated outside US-EAST without explicit written approval from MedSys. (Security: verify backup vendors; some infra partners may have metadata replicated for availability — we can provide a data residency attestation.)

Attachments to include in reply to MedSys: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (redacted summary of SOC 2 Type II) and redwood-privacy-addendum-v1.docx (sample addendum). subprocessors-202808.csv is attached for transparency.

Suggested next step to Julia: confirm whether MedSys wants us to: (a) propose edits inline on their DPA template, or (b) sign their template as-is and attach our addendum. Also propose a 30-minute call with Legal/Privacy and BizOps (Mark Hansen) tomorrow to finalize.

Thanks — Dev
Head of Security Engineering
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com

Hi Julia / Mark — thanks again. Per Dev and Legal, here are concise answers and the attachments you requested. Please see the attached redwood-privacy-addendum-v1.docx and redwood-soc2-summary.pdf plus the subprocessors export. I summarized below so procurement has a single message to review: 

- Controller / Processor: MedSys Health is the Controller; Redwood is the Processor for hosted inference. Redwood separately collects aggregated telemetry as a service-controller, but telemetry excludes PII/prompt content unless you opt in.

- Subprocessors: current list attached. All subprocessors have flow-down DPAs. We provide 30 days advance notice for additions by default; longer notice can be discussed for enterprise contracts.

- Breach notification: standard commitment is initial notification within 72 hours for incidents materially affecting customer data. 48-hour initial notification is negotiable for enterprise deals with Legal/Security sign-off; please flag if you require 48h as a hard requirement. Full forensic reports will follow the investigation.

- Logs & forensic exports: default 30-day retention. Options: 90-day or 365-day retention as paid add-ons. Export includes request IDs, timestamps, model/route metadata and system identifiers; payloads (prompt contents) are retained only if explicitly enabled by you. For 180-day retention, Sales Ops will provide a precise price—rough estimate +15% storage/billing.

- Residency: we can pin MedSys workloads and data-at-rest to US-EAST. Backups remain in-region unless you provide explicit written approval to replicate elsewhere. We will provide a data-residency attestation and redacted SOC2 report for procurement.

Next step: Would you prefer we (A) propose inline edits to your DPA template, or (B) sign your template and append our addendum? Also, if it helps, we can do a 30-minute call tomorrow with Legal / BizOps (Dev, Marissa, Laura + your Mark) to move to PO. 

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.
